subtitulo: If you were in charge of the office
descripcion: The second conditional talks about an unreal present or future: if I had more time, I would travel more. The form is fixed and the meaning is clear once the pattern is automatic — the challenge at B2 is using it fluently in real hypotheticals, not just in isolated drills.

filas: I could learn a new language.

ejemplos.texto: If I had more time, I would travel much more.
If she knew about it, she would say something.
I could learn a new instrument if I weren't so busy.

notas: Were is used instead of was with I/he/she/it in careful English: if I were you, though was is common in speech.
Would never appears in the if-clause: if I would have time is not standard English.
Could and might replace would to express ability or possibility rather than a definite result.

contraste.es: Spanish uses si + imperfecto de subjuntivo and the simple conditional (si tuviera tiempo, viajaría), with a logic parallel to English. Standard Spanish does not put the conditional after si, although some regional varieties do (si tendría tiempo); speakers of those varieties are especially prone to if I would have more time.
contraste.de: German has the same logic (Wenn ich mehr Zeit hätte, würde ich mehr reisen), but colloquial German also allows würde in the wenn-clause. German speakers therefore often produce if I would have more time, the single most frequent error with this structure.
contraste.it: Italian has the same logic (se avessi più tempo, viaggerei di più) and no conditional after se in the standard language, so the structure transfers well. Colloquial Italian, however, often uses the imperfetto in both halves (se avevo tempo, viaggiavo), which can produce I travelled more instead of I would travel more.
contraste.fr: French has the same logic, and si + imparfait (si j'avais plus de temps) corresponds exactly to if + past simple. Because French does not allow the conditional after si, French speakers rarely put would in the if-clause, which makes this one of the easier structures for them.
contraste.pt: Portuguese has the same logic (se tivesse mais tempo, viajaria mais). In colloquial European Portuguese the imperfeito often replaces the conditional (viajava mais), which can produce I travelled more instead of I would travel more.

errores: Using would in the if-clause: if I would have more time.
Using was instead of were in formal writing with I/he/she/it.
Mixing the second conditional with the first: if I would have time, I will travel.

es: Copying the colloquial imperfect (*si tuviera tiempo, iba*): *If I had time, I went* instead of *I would go*.
de: *wenn* rendered as *when* for a hypothesis: *When I had more time, I would travel* instead of *If I had more time*.
it: *se fossi in te* rendered as *If I were in you* instead of *If I were you*.
fr: *au cas où* + conditional rendered as *In case he would come* instead of *In case he comes*.
pt: Copying the colloquial imperfect (*se tivesse tempo, ia*): *If I had time, I went* instead of *I would go*.

redemittel.expresion: Is this hypothetical or just unlikely?
redemittel.funcion: checks which conditional the situation needs

traducciones.es: ¿Esto es hipotético o solo poco probable?
traducciones.de: Ist das hypothetisch oder nur unwahrscheinlich?
traducciones.fr: Est-ce hypothétique ou seulement peu probable ?
traducciones.pt: Isto é hipotético ou apenas pouco provável?

mision.consigna: Describe how you would change one public office or service if you were in charge of it.
requisitos: one question with *What would you do if…?*
use *to fill in a form*, *deadline* and *to be in charge of*

microtareas.texto: Five sentences: *If I were in charge of…, I would…*.
Three pieces of advice with *If I were you* for someone applying for a *certificate*.
Record 90 seconds: what would you change about *customer service* in your country?

autochequeo: Is the if-clause in the past simple, with no would inside it?
Is were used instead of was in formal contexts?
Does the main clause use would, could or might correctly?
Is the situation genuinely unreal, not a real future possibility?
Have I avoided mixing the first and second conditional in the same sentence?
promptCorreccion: Focus only on the second conditional. Check for would inside the if-clause, check were versus was, and check whether would, could or might is used correctly in the main clause. Do not rewrite the text.
